newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui, GE win Thai power plant order.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui, GE win Thai power plant order.

text.p: Mitsui & Co said on Friday that it and General Electric Co of the United States had jointly won an order to build an electric power plant in Thailand.
The plant, which is to be built for Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand, will have a total output capacity of 2.1 million kilowatts, Mitsui said in a statement.
The construction of all of the plant facilities will be completed by March 2000, the statement said.
A Mitsui spokesman declined to give the value of the order.
The power plant will feature a combined-cycle system in which heat from gas turbines is used to power steam turbines, allowing for the efficient use of gas fuel, the statement said.
General Electric will manufacture the turbines, while Mitsui is to manage the procurement of other equipment, it said.
The Mitsui spokesman said it and Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding Co Ltd had also won a 10 billion yen order to build an electric power plant in Malaysia last month.
